title: ETS Pattern Matching, Match Specs (select, select_delete) & protected Reads
solutionExplanation: Uses {keypos, 2} to index records by token and compiles match specifications for select and atomic select_delete.

otpDocCards.description: Atomically deletes all records matching the match specification from table Tab inside ERTS C memory.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(N) table scan executing entirely in off-heap C memory.

otpDocCards.description: Searches the table Tab using a match specification, returning only matching rows transformed to the result format.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(N) scan without copying non-matching terms to process heap.

otpDocCards.description: Returns all objects in table Tab that match the specified tuple pattern containing _ wildcards.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(N) scan for set; O(log N) if key is fixed.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why is using ets:select_delete/2 superior to fetching records with ets:tab2list/1, filtering in Erlang, and calling ets:delete/2 in a loop?

options.label: tab2list/1 encrypts the data before returning it to the Erlang process.
ets:select_delete/2 evaluates filters and frees rows directly in the C runtime without copying millions of terms to the process heap.
options.explanation: tab2list/1 copies every single tuple out of off-heap C memory and onto the calling process heap, generating massive garbage collection pressure. ets:select_delete/2 filters and deletes rows directly in C memory.

options.label: ets:delete/2 does not work on named tables.
options.explanation: ets:delete/2 works fine on named tables.

options.label: tab2list/1 automatically deletes the ETS table after being called.
